messages:
anya: quick sync — i think we're still fuzzy on which side should own prewarm decisions for dedicated GPU pools: control plane (intent) vs operator (node lifecycle). thoughts?

matt: my take: control plane should own the policy (when to prewarm) and provide an intent + ttl. operator should just execute lifecycle ops and expose metrics/backpressure. keep policy in control plane to avoid operator churn.

ryan: agree mostly, but operator needs a small admission surface (admit/reject + token) so it can protect node stability. otherwise control plane could thrash the node layer during noisy spikes.

sasha: +1. we also need a clear contract for graceful failure. e.g., operator returns `INSUFFICIENT_HEADROOM` + suggested retry-after. control plane translates to routing/fallback.

jen: question: how do we handle cost attribution? if control plane decides to prewarm but operator delays, who gets charged/metrics attributed? we need idempotent reservations.

anya: propose an "intent ticket" model: control plane creates an intent object with owner, budget tag, desired size, prewarm TTL, and priority. operator consumes ticket and returns status updates (ACCEPTED/QUEUED/PROVISIONED/REJECTED).

matt: that maps well to current CRD approach. But make ticket lightweight (no heavy reconciliation fields). operator should be able to garbage-collect stale tickets based on TTL.

ryan: implementation nit: ticket should include a `soft_live_by` timestamp and a `probe_window_ms`. operator can probe cached nodes before launching new ones — reduces churn.

sasha: admission tokens + probe window seems fine. also require operator to expose per-tenant headroom metric and a `prewarm_backpressure` gauge. control plane can use that to decide fallback to hosted or lower-quality quantized variants.

jen: migration concern: existing autoscaler relies on a single `desired_count` API. migrating to ticket model needs a compatibility shim for older controllers during a rollout.

anya: plan: (1) add ticket API on control plane (gRPC + REST), (2) operator implements ticket consumer + minimal admission surface, (3) add transition shim to translate existing desired_count to ephemeral tickets, (4) feature flag rollout.

matt: also: operator should prefer warm caches (KV caches) on provisioned nodes. include an optional `cache_hint` field in the ticket: e.g., `prefixes:[...], expected_seq_len:512`.

ryan: ops-bot: deploy-check integrated? ops-bot: new endpoint added to control-plane: /v1/autoscale/tickets (POST) — returns ticket_id. Operator polls / streams tickets.

sasha: edge-case: race between ticket expiration and node provisioning. require operator to extend ticket with `heartbeat` call when it starts provisioning; control plane can extend TTL if budget exists.

jen: testing: add e2e that simulates slow provisioning and ensures fallback path triggers (route to hosted pool). also add unit tests for ticket lifecycle and metrics emission.

anya: wanted tradeoff note in thread: putting policy in control plane centralizes ML+telemetry usage for prediction, but increases control plane load and adds latency for rapid bursts. operator-local heuristics can be allowed as a low-priority fast path.

matt: reconcile with SLOs: control plane policy decisions must be bounded by X ms (TBD) or we provide immediate best-effort tickets with `priority=fast` which tells operator it can apply local heuristics.

ryan: security: tickets must carry a tenant sig/nonce to prevent replay and to enable auditing. operator should log ticket_id and decisions for billing reconciliation.

sasha: ops TODOs: add prewarm_backpressure metric, ticket heartbeating endpoint, and quick rejection codes. I'll own operator changes.

jen: control plane TODOs: ticket API, migration shim, priority semantics, and RFC writeup. i'll draft RFC and own rollout plan.

anya: ok owner notes captured. follow-ups: jen to RFC, sasha to operator PR, matt to add fallback routing for hosted pool, ryan to write tests. sync next Wed.

matt: thanks — this feels actionable. :thumbsup:
